metadata.description: A host's baseboard management controller — its management address, protocol, and the power/reset control surface — modeled so power actions have a first-class target. Every board vendor ships its own BMC family; this record is vendor-neutral. Credentials are never inline (reference a Security.CredentialRef). `manages` points at the host it powers; power operations are Redfish (or a vendor tool like ipmitool where a board's Redfish is incomplete) — the mechanism is Policy (the control plane), not data.

protocol.description: Out-of-band protocol(s) the BMC answers. redfish for power/reset; ipmi as legacy fallback.

vendor.description: BMC/board vendor — the observed vendor string (e.g. `<vendor>`).

power_state.description: Last-observed chassis power state (On/Off) from Redfish ComputerSystem.PowerState.

relationships.description: The host this BMC is the out-of-band controller for — its power/reset surface. A BMC controls exactly one host when assigned.

adopts.role: management-controller data model + the power-control action vocabulary UDLM references, never restates

context.purpose: Models a host's baseboard management controller so power and reset actions have a first-class, addressable target.
context.plain_description: The always-on management controller inside a server that answers even when the host is off — each board vendor ships its own flavor. This record carries its `management_address`, the single `protocol` it answers — `redfish`, `ipmi`, or the combined `redfish+ipmi` — and its `vendor`, and points at the one host it controls. Credentials are never stored here — they are referenced. It exists so that power that host off resolves to a concrete address and mechanism instead of prose.
use_when: You need out-of-band power/reset control of a host to be addressable data, for shutdown ordering and recovery automation.
You need the management-network surface of the fleet inventoried separately from in-band host addresses.
not_for: The host itself — Compute.BareMetalHost; the BMC manages it, one-to-one.
The BMC login secret — Security.CredentialRef, referenced not stored.
works_with: Compute.BareMetalHost — the host this BMC is the power/reset surface for.
Security.CredentialRef — the BMC credential, by reference.
Hardware.BiosProfile — firmware profiles applied over the BMC's out-of-band path.
